text:
maya: quick thought — do we want explicit model identity claims in the rollout payloads? e.g. a small, typed `identity` block separate from pins or aliases
akshay: what do you mean by claims? like issuer + fingerprint + semantic tag?
sam: +1 on having something typed. we've been leaning on pins but clients keep reading pins as the canonical id which leaks internal semantics
jonah: concern: any extra fields increase surface area for clients to rely on. hard to remove later. :thinking:
maya: agreed. tradeoff is: typed claims let us evolve mapping logic server-side (shim conversions) and keep rollout decision deterministic
akshay: can you sketch the minimal shape?
maya: something like:
```
"identity": {
  "kind": "assertion",        // assertion | alias | provenance
  "id": "sha256:...",       // canonical hash
  "label": "redwood/v1/gptx-small", // human label (optional)
  "issued_by": "catalog-service", // who minted the claim
}
```
jonah: that looks strict. what about TTL / revocation? where does that live?
sam: probably keep lifecycle fields in rollout metadata separate (expiry, grace_window), we don't want to conflate identity with lifecycle policy
maya: right — identity = stable claim, lifecycle = policy. shim idea: when a legacy pin arrives we synthesize an identity claim with kind=alias + provenance pointing at the pin and record provenance in audit logs
akshay: operational concern: if we start emitting identity in responses, client SDKs might cache based on it. we should be explicit about which fields are safe to cache and for how long
jonah: suggestion: add a `client_contracts` field in the rollout manifest describing cache TTL and whether clients may persist the identity
maya: hmm i'd rather not invent another DSL in rollout. simpler: allow `identity.cacheable: "true|false"` and `identity.cache_ttl_seconds` as optional hints
sam: small nit — prefer boolean not string for cacheable, but DSL restrictions aside i get it. remember agents.md constraints :P
ops-bot: deploy-check: schema change requires console + sdk bump, will block minor release if not flagged
akshay: given the ops note, path of least surprise: introduce identity as optional, server-side shim maps existing pins/aliases into identity, and we add a conservative `cacheable:false` by default
jonah: also add a compatibility header `X-Model-Identity-V1` to responses so we can gate rollouts and A/B test without changing body parsing for old clients
maya: love that. header-based opt-in for early clients, body field for new clients. then we can flip the header off once SDKs adopt
sam: one more: telemetry — include identity.id in rollout traces but hash before sending to third-party sinks (PII concern)
akshay: yep, scrubbed hashing + provenance id is fine
jonah: i'll write a short RFC follow-up with example manifests and a migration plan (shim impl + header flag + sdk note). can someone volunteer to prototype the shim?
maya: i can take a spike next week, will prototype conversion and header emission
jonah: i'll own the SDK change after the spike
sam: ok, file the RFC follow-up and put a blocker on the next minor until we have tests for shim edgecases
maya: filed: https://go/rfcs/2026-model-identity-shim (draft) — pinging infra for review
ops-bot: noted. scheduled a 30m sync on Friday to review the draft
maya: thanks — we'll capture decisions in the RFC and keep identity optional by default. end of thread.
